samples.summary: Materializing `lineAffinity: 'backward'` on every caret position defeats `buildRects`' "start endpoint with no affinity reads forward" rule for keyboard-built selection anchors
samples.evidence: `buildRects` (packages/docs/src/view/selection.ts:260-261) deliberately distinguishes *absent* from *present* affinity: `const startAffinity = start.lineAffinity ?? 'forward'` — the comment and docs/design/docs/docs-local-caret-anchoring.md:84-87 say an endpoint carrying none must read forward "rather than opening on a zero-width sliver of the line above". Every keyboard-built selection anchor is taken straight from the caret: text-editor.ts:2948 (`const anchor = this.selection.range?.anchor ?? pos`, where `pos = this.cursor.position` at 2629), and the same pattern at text-editor.ts:2981 (handleHome), 3000 (handleEnd), 3015 (handleDocStart), 3031 (handleDocEnd), 1746 and 1794 (shift+click). Before this change `cursor.position` carried no `lineAffinity`, so those anchors hit the `?? 'forward'` branch. After the change the constructor (cursor.ts:26) and `moveTo` (cursor.ts:52-56) always stamp one, so a caret that sits exactly on a wrap boundary with the default 'backward' reading now hands the selection an explicit 'backward' start — the highlight starts at the end of the previous visual line and paints the sliver the forward default existed to avoid. Nothing catches it: selection-line-affinity.test.ts hand-builds positions rather than driving the caret, and the new caret-line-affinity.test.ts only asserts the published affinity value, not the rects. Fix belongs either at the new materialization site (only stamp when a reading was actually determined) or by making the anchor sites strip/choose the endpoint reading explicitly.

samples.summary: `getPixelForPosition` still hardcodes a `'backward'` default, bypassing the new "omit it to use the position's own reading" contract — link-popover rect anchors to the wrong visual line
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:5307 declares `private getPixelForPosition(pos: DocPosition, lineAffinity: 'forward' | 'backward' = 'backward')` and forwards that value into `resolvePositionPixel`. Because it passes an explicit `'backward'`, the fallback the diff added at peer-cursor.ts:111 (`lineAffinity ?? position.lineAffinity ?? 'backward'`) never applies here. The callers that omit the argument pass caret positions that now carry an affinity: text-editor.ts:5472 `this.getPixelForPosition(cursorPos)` with `cursorPos = this.cursor.position` (5444), plus 5468-5469 for the link run bounds. A caret sitting on a wrap boundary with forward affinity therefore gets a link-popover rect one visual line above the caret — exactly the mismatch the diff fixed for peer carets (editor.ts:1586) and `scrollToPosition` (editor.ts:2841) but left in place here.

samples.summary: `TextBoxEditorAPI.onCursorMove` still declares the old `{blockId, offset}` shape while the runtime now hands out an affinity-carrying position
samples.evidence: The diff widened the docs `EditorAPI.onCursorMove` to `(pos: DocPosition, selection?: DocRange | null)` (editor.ts:128) but the sibling text-box API left behind still declares `onCursorMove(cb: (pos: { blockId: string; offset: number }, selection?: { anchor: {blockId,offset}; focus: {blockId,offset} } | null) => void)` at packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:329 and :1289, and it dispatches `cursorMoveCallback(cursor.position, selRange)` (text-box-editor.ts:617, 648) — a `Cursor` position that now always carries `lineAffinity`. Slides consumers (packages/slides/src/view/editor/text-box-editor.ts:283, packages/slides/src/view/editor/editor.ts:4225) therefore cannot see the field the docs cursor now publishes, so the type documents a contract the implementation no longer has.

samples.summary: Affinity now lives inside `cursor.position`, so the text-box editor's JSON dedupe key changes on affinity-only caret moves and fires extra cursor-move fan-out into slides
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:614 computes `const key = JSON.stringify({ cur: cursor.position, sel: selRange })` (and :647 stores it) to suppress duplicate `onCursorMove` notifications. With `lineAffinity` moved inside `position` (cursor.ts:26/38/52) a move that changes only the wrap-boundary reading now produces a different key, so the callback fires where it previously did not. The downstream consumer is slides' cell-boundary navigation handler (packages/slides/src/view/editor/editor.ts:4225) and the toolbar refresh subscribers fanned out at packages/slides/src/view/editor/text-box-editor.ts:652-657, neither of which was considered in this change.

samples.summary: Ruler page lookup still resolves the caret with `findPageForPosition`'s hardcoded `'backward'` default while the caret is drawn with its own affinity
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1923-1925 calls `findPageForPosition(paginatedLayout, cursor.position.blockId, cursor.position.offset, layout)` with no affinity argument, and pagination.ts:385 defaults that parameter to `'backward'`. Now that the caret carries its own reading and the peer/scroll paths were switched to honour it, this fallback path (taken when `cursorPixel` is undefined) can pick the page of the line *above* the one the caret is drawn on, giving the ruler the wrong page's margins for a forward-affinity caret at a page-boundary wrap.

samples.summary: Peer-cursor change detection keys on `blockId:offset` only, so a peer's affinity-only caret move no longer matches what is now published
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-view.tsx:284 builds `const posKey = `${presence.activeCursorPos.blockId}:${presence.activeCursorPos.offset}`` to decide whether a peer's caret moved (label re-show + timer reset). `activeCursorPos` now always carries `lineAffinity` (published by `updateCursorPos` at yorkie-doc-store.ts:3053 and `recordHistoryPresence` at :2950), and a peer caret that changes only its wrap-boundary reading is re-rendered at a different y (editor.ts:1586) without the label logic noticing. Cosmetic only — `setPeerCursors(buildPeerCursors())` still runs on every presence change (docs-view.tsx:315).

samples.summary: Local caret anchors now always store an affinity, so `restoreLocalCursor` re-applies a stale wrap-boundary reading after remote edits change the wrapping
samples.evidence: `updateCursorPos` anchors the caret with `this.anchorDocPosition(clampedPos, clampedPos.lineAffinity)` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:3048), and `resolveAnchoredDocPosition` re-attaches it (:1077). Previously keyboard-moved carets published no affinity, so the anchor stored none and the resolved position fell back to 'backward'; now every caret stores one. The resolved position feeds `restoreLocalCursor` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts ~3647), which the diff changed to spread it wholesale, so a remote edit that rewraps the paragraph can now restore a 'forward' reading at an offset that is no longer a wrap boundary. Confirming this needs a remote-edit rewrap scenario; the existing anchor tests hand-build positions.

verdict.reason: The mechanism is present exactly as described and I could not refute it on any named ground. cursor.ts:26 and cursor.ts:52-56 always materialize `lineAffinity` (defaulting to 'backward'), and selection.ts:260-261 still treats an absent start affinity as meaningful (`start.lineAffinity ?? 'forward'`), a rule also stated in docs/design/docs/docs-local-caret-anchoring.md:83-87. normalizeRange (selection.ts:115-172) passes endpoint objects through untouched, so the explicit 'backward' reaches `startAffinity`. The anchor sites cited are real (text-editor.ts:2948 with pos = cursor.position at 2629; 2981, 3000, 3015, 3031, 1746, 1794) and the `?? this.cursor.position` fallback is reachable because an unshifted arrow nulls the range at text-editor.ts:2968 and left motion sets 'backward' at 2944. Impact is not purely theoretical: in the cell-internal branch the start affinity selects startLineIdx (selection.ts:337-366) and the start rect is painted from startPixel.x to cellRightX (selection.ts:427-429), so a backward-read anchor highlights the trailing gap of the previous visual line. Residual doubt (hence low confidence): in the non-cell branch the extra first rect is effectively zero width (selection.ts:503-509), and docs-local-caret-anchoring.md:96-98 documents the always-materialized caret reading as intentional — so the practical severity is arguable. But arguable severity is not a refutation ground, and no guard or caller makes the path unreachable.

finding.summary: Cursor.position now always materializes a lineAffinity, which defeats the out-of-diff "selection start defaults to forward" rule wherever a shift-selection anchor falls back to the caret
finding.evidence: `buildRects` (packages/docs/src/view/selection.ts:260-261) relies on an *absent* affinity to apply the asymmetric default: `const startAffinity = start.lineAffinity ?? 'forward'`. Before this change a keyboard-derived caret position carried no `lineAffinity` (Cursor.moveTo stored `pos` verbatim and kept the affinity in a sibling field), so anchors built from the caret hit that default. After the change `cursor.position` always has one (cursor.ts:26/39/55). The anchor fallbacks are all out of the diff: packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2774 (`const anchor = this.selection.range?.anchor ?? pos`), :2807 (shift+Home), :2826 (shift+End), :2841, :2857 — each now hands `buildRects` a start endpoint carrying the caret's reading (typically `'backward'` after typing or ArrowLeft, `'forward'` after ArrowRight). `getNormalizedRange` returns endpoints as stored (selection.ts:705), so a shift-selection begun at a wrap boundary now paints its first rect on the previous visual line / as a zero-width sliver — exactly the artefact the comment at selection.ts:255-259 says the default exists to prevent. The same normalized endpoints are published to presence, so peers see it too. Fix likely belongs on the new code (do not materialize `'backward'` on carets that never chose one, or make the anchor fallback drop the caret's affinity).

verdict.reason: Every element of the finding checks out against the repository. buildRects keys its asymmetric default on an ABSENT affinity (selection.ts:260-261, with the comment at :255-259 stating why start must read 'forward'), while Cursor now always materializes one (cursor.ts:26, :39, :55, documented at :12-19). The anchor fallbacks that feed that default are out of the diff and unchanged: text-editor.ts:2948 (pos = this.cursor.position at :2629), :2981, :3000, :3015, :3031, plus :1746/:1794 — and they pass the anchor through verbatim even where the focus affinity is explicitly set (:2952, :2987). setRange (selection.ts:690-692) and normalizeRange (selection.ts:166-179) return endpoints as stored, and computeSelectionRects hands them straight to buildRects (selection.ts:554-564); no consumer I grepped (editor.ts:1565/1645/1665/1684/1701/3177, text-box-editor.ts:560) normalizes the start endpoint. Reachable: hAffinity at text-editor.ts:2944 leaves the caret 'backward' after ArrowLeft and the constructor default is 'backward', so a shift-selection begun on a wrap boundary now resolves its start pixel to the end of the previous visual line. Only the reviewer's line numbers were off (2774/2807/2826/2841/2857 vs the real 2948/2981/3000/3015/3031) — a citation drift within the same file, not a misdescription of the code. This is a contract/nullability change on an exported symbol breaking an out-of-diff consumer, i.e. in-lane and major.
